title: Gate-charge average supply current and drive power
description: Estimate the cycle-average current and power drawn from a unipolar gate-driver supply by one MOSFET's gate charge.
formula: I_supply = Q_g f_sw; E_drive = Q_g V_drive; P_drive = E_drive f_sw
assumptions: One complete 0 V to V_drive to 0 V gate cycle per switching period; no energy-recovery driver or negative gate bias.
Q_g must come from a gate-charge curve at the actual drive voltage, drain voltage and load current; do not substitute C_iss V_drive.
Supply current is Q_g f_sw, not 2 Q_g f_sw: gate discharge flows through the sink path rather than drawing a second Q_g from the positive supply.
Power is dissipated across the driver, external resistor and MOSFET internal gate resistance, not wholly in the MOSFET channel. Driver quiescent and shoot-through consumption are excluded.

references.title: Infineon OptiMOS device selection for synchronous rectification, equation 7

inputs.label: Total gate charge at operating point

title: Gate-loop critical-damping resistor selection
description: Size the minimum nonnegative external series gate resistance that brings a lumped gate loop to at least critical damping.
formula: R_critical = 2 sqrt(L_loop/C_iss); R_external = max(0, R_critical - R_driver - R_internal); zeta = (R_driver + R_internal + R_external)/R_critical
assumptions: The initial gate charging loop is a linear series RLC network with lumped loop/source inductance and locally appropriate C_iss.
Use driver output resistance for the edge under study. Source and sink resistances can differ; this is not a current-limited driver model.
If existing resistance exceeds critical resistance, zero added resistance is returned and zeta exceeds one; no passive resistor can restore exact critical damping.
This is a ringing/damping design estimate, not Miller-time selection or a guarantee of EMI, gate-voltage safety or switching performance.
Voltage-dependent capacitance, common-source feedback and distributed parasitics require measured waveform confirmation.

references.title: Texas Instruments SLUA618A, section 2.8, Figure 7 and equation 15

inputs.label: Driver resistance for the selected edge

title: Bootstrap capacitance from gate and driver charge budget
description: Find the theoretical minimum effective bootstrap capacitance for a specified droop, accounting for gate charge, high-side leakage and full-cycle quiescent consumption.
formula: Q_total = Q_g + I_hbs D_max/f_sw + I_hb/f_sw; V_headroom = V_dd - V_diode - V_min; C_min = Q_total/Delta_V
assumptions: TI SLUA887A charge-budget convention: HB-to-VSS leakage acts for D_max/f_sw; high-side quiescent current is budgeted conservatively over the full 1/f_sw period.
Floating supply initially charges to approximately V_dd - V_diode; the switch node is near ground during recharge and the capacitor is replenished once each cycle.
V_min is the larger required floating supply voltage from driver UVLO plus desired margin and MOSFET adequate gate enhancement, entered by the designer.
Droop must be positive and no larger than V_dd - V_diode - V_min. Duty must be strictly between zero and one; 100 percent duty needs another supply mechanism.
C_min is effective capacitance at bias and temperature, not the nominal printed value. Add tolerance, aging, DC-bias and transient margin when selecting a real part.

Driver current definitions vary; use the selected driver's datasheet. Unbudgeted level-shifter charge, gate/capacitor/diode leakage, skipped pulses, recharge impedance, ESR and ESL can require a larger capacitor.

references.title: Texas Instruments SLUA887A Bootstrap Circuitry Selection for Half-Bridge Configurations, section 3.1, equation 3

constraints.message: The initial bootstrap voltage must exceed the minimum floating supply voltage.
Allowed droop cannot exceed available supply headroom.

title: MOSFET output-capacitance hard turn-on loss
description: Estimate the energy dumped from a MOSFET's nonlinear output capacitance into its channel at hard turn-on using energy-equivalent capacitance.
formula: E_oss = C_o_er V_ds^2/2; P_oss = E_oss f_sw
assumptions: C_o_er is energy-related effective output capacitance for the complete 0 V to entered V_ds swing, defined by 2 E_oss(V_ds)/V_ds^2.
Never use a single small-signal C_oss point or time-related C_o_tr as C_o_er. A value characterized at a different drain voltage must be replaced with the appropriate curve value.
One complete hard discharge of the selected MOSFET's output capacitance into its channel occurs per switching cycle, with no energy recovery.
This is only the selected device's stored-energy discharge term, not total converter output-capacitance charging loss or a synchronous rectifier V Q_oss - E_oss model.
Zero-voltage/resonant switching can recycle this energy. Reverse recovery, external capacitors and overlap loss are excluded.
Do not add this to measured switching energies that already include output-capacitance loss.

references.title: Infineon 600 V CoolMOS C7 Design Guide, section 3.4, Figures 9-12
Infineon OptiMOS device selection for synchronous rectification, equation 19, nonlinear stored-energy integral

inputs.label: Energy-equivalent output capacitance at entered voltage

title: MOSFET conduction loss with on-state current ripple
description: Compute full-cycle channel RMS current and conduction loss for a duty-gated, linearly ramping positive current.
formula: I_rms = sqrt(D (I_mean^2 + Delta_I_pp^2/12)); P_cond = I_rms^2 R_ds_on
assumptions: Channel current is zero outside duty fraction D. During the on interval it traverses uniformly between I_mean - Delta_I_pp/2 and I_mean + Delta_I_pp/2.
I_mean is the average during the on interval, not the average drain current over the whole cycle. Ripple is peak-to-peak.
Current stays nonnegative; discontinuous conduction with a zero-current subinterval requires a different waveform model.
R_ds_on is supplied at the actual gate voltage and junction temperature. No temperature calculation or feedback is performed.
Body-diode conduction, dead time and switching losses are excluded.

references.title: Infineon OptiMOS device selection for synchronous rectification, section 3.2, equation 5

inputs.label: Mean current during channel on interval

constraints.message: The triangular current minimum must be nonnegative.
